requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) configured with 802.1Q sub-interfaces for VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 acting as router between them
requirements.summary: eth1.10 (10.10.10.254/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.254/24) VLAN sub-interfaces were created via configure/commit/save and directly observed active with correct 802.1Q tags (cmd-712e0de344ee4e69, cmd-e4855a1fb9f64a6a). Persistence confirmed post-restart with unchanged config and interfaces up (cmd-347b4565b7124904, cmd-5a53aa4bb28d4460).

requirements.requirement: node2 placed on VLAN 10 over the shared link
requirements.summary: NetworkManager VLAN connection vlan10 created on eth1.10 with address 10.10.10.11/24, activated and confirmed in ip -br addr and nmcli active connections (cmd-d955ea1d78124b9f, cmd-1974da6973e9457f). Confirmed still active post-restart (cmd-edea612c415349e5).

requirements.requirement: node3 placed on VLAN 20 over the shared link
requirements.summary: NetworkManager VLAN connection vlan20 created on eth1.20 with address 10.10.20.12/24, activated (cmd-c1f4574272df42cc, cmd-9cabfbd9853a47e9). Confirmed still active post-restart (cmd-3ac174920a5745a9).

requirements.requirement: Routing between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 works through node1, and the two systems remain isolated on the raw untagged shared link
requirements.summary: IP forwarding confirmed enabled on node1 (cmd-4f1a2e1453ca4f6d). Bidirectional cross-VLAN ping succeeded with ttl=63 (one hop, consistent with routing via node1) both node2->node3 and node3->node2 (cmd-ea90cae1bf7648d6, cmd-fb9cad86f1c5427a). Direct ping attempt over the untagged eth1 path failed (100% loss), directly demonstrating VLAN separation on the shared link (cmd-cb1d0080760645f6).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol demonstrating VLAN/routing configuration survives restart on all three nodes
requirements.summary: All three nodes show a full bounded disruption cycle: pre-restart boot-id and healthy VLAN/route state, restart trigger, a distinct post-restart boot-id, and re-verified interfaces/routes/forwarding, followed by a successful cross-VLAN ping confirming functional recovery. Post-restart boot-ids (f94aa3ca, 5750ce04, d4d90ac8) match the fixed after_executor lifecycle snapshot, cross-checking the executor's claims.

overall_summary: The executor correctly implemented VLAN 10/20 segmentation of node2/node3 over the shared eth1 link with node1 (VyOS) routing between the VLANs via 802.1Q sub-interfaces and IP forwarding. Direct evidence shows successful cross-VLAN ping (ttl=63) confirming routing through node1, and a failed ping over the untagged shared link confirming VLAN isolation. All configuration was persisted, and the mandated restart protocol was executed and verified on all three nodes with distinct pre/post boot-ids and full functional recovery, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: Restart-triggering commands on node2 and node3 returned non-zero/exec-stream-closed outcomes, which is expected behavior when a reboot terminates the exec session mid-command rather than a task failure.

The NetworkManager-wait-online.service failure observed post-restart on node2 was not investigated or explained by the executor; it does not appear to have degraded VLAN/routing functionality (subsequent ping succeeded) but is an unexplained state change worth noting.

VyOS firewall/NAT check (cmd-b7cc0bcfa2704647) showed empty configuration, supporting that no additional filtering rules blocked routing, but this was inferred rather than an explicit permit rule being tested against a deny-by-default posture.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task outcomes or the restart protocol; one early failed troubleshooting attempt (cmd-5e2a055d93cd4a19, missing VyOS operational-mode shell wrapper) made no state change and was immediately corrected. Minor unreverted residue: /tmp/reboot.log left on node2 and node3 from the reboot trigger commands (bounded, low-risk, single small file, visible in after_executor temp-file diffs). One notable but likely environment-driven artifact: node2's after_executor snapshot shows NetworkManager-wait-online.service in a failed state, not present at baseline; this is plausibly a side effect of the VLAN interface bring-up race during boot rather than a deliberate executor mutation, but it is a change in service health that was not addressed or explained by the executor.
